title: Etale neighbourhood of a maximal fibre degree point is finite locally free
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Suppose $m\in\mathbb N$ bounds its finite fibre degrees [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]. Let $s\in S$ have fibre degree $m$. There exist a scheme $T$, an etale morphism $\varphi:T\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and a point $t\in T$ with $\varphi(t)=s$ such that the projection $X\times_S T\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is finite locally free of degree $m$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

proof.text: *Set-up at the specified point of maximal degree.* Fix $s\in S_m$. The fibre $X_s$ is finite over $\kappa(s)$, so $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ has finite fibres [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] (2), i.e. $X_s$ is a finite set; the first projection is a homeomorphism of $X_s$ onto $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], so $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is finite and $X_s$ has at most finitely many isolated points. As $f$ is locally of finite presentation it is locally of finite type (a finitely presented algebra is finitely generated: [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]), and it is separated. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-splits-off-quasi-finite-part] there are an elementary etale neighbourhood $\varphi:(U,u)\to(S,s)$ ($\varphi$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]) and a decomposition $U\times_SX=W\sqcup V$ into disjoint open subschemes with $V\to U$ finite and $W_u=\emptyset$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RY (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-lqf-universally-bounded), line 12761, proof, second paragraph ('Choose an elementary etale morphism (U,u) -> (S,s) and a decomposition U x_S X = W amalg V as in Lemma 02LP')

proof.text: *$V\to U$ is finite locally free.* The projection $U\times_SX\to U$ is the base change of $f$ along $\varphi$, hence flat and locally of finite presentation (step 1). $V$ is an open subscheme of $U\times_SX$: for $v\in V$ the local ring $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ is $\mathcal O_{U\times_SX,v}$, so $V\to U$ is flat at $v$ [def-weil-flat-morphism], and the affine opens around $v$ with finitely presented ring maps given by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] may be shrunk to standard opens $D(a)$ inside $V$ (a localization $B_a$ of a finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$ is finitely presented, $B_a=B[x]/(ax-1)$), so $V\to U$ is locally of finite presentation. Being also finite, $V\to U$ is finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free] (finite, flat and locally of finite presentation; this is Stacks Morphisms, Lemma 02KB, which here is the definition).

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RY (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-lqf-universally-bounded), line 12761, proof, second paragraph ('Since V -> U is finite, flat, and locally of finite presentation, we see that V -> U is finite locally free, see Morphisms, Lemma 02KB')

proof.text: *Shrinking $U$; the degree at $u$ is $m$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-locally-constant] the degree function $\delta_{V\to U}$ is locally constant; let $d=\delta_{V\to U}(u)$ and $U'=\delta_{V\to U}^{-1}(d)$, an open (and closed) neighbourhood of $u$ over which the preimage of $U'$ in $V$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ (Stacks Morphisms, Lemma 04MH). Replace $U$ by $U'$, and $W,V$ by their preimages $W',V'$ under $U'\times_SX\to U'$; by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] $U'\times_SX$ is the preimage of $U'$ in $U\times_SX$ and $U'\times_SX=W'\sqcup V'$ with $V'\to U'$ finite locally free of degree $d$, $W'_u=\emptyset$; $U'\to S$ is etale as the composite of the open immersion $U'\to U$ and $\varphi$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), (2), and $\kappa(u)$ is unchanged. The fibre $(U'\times_SX)_u$ has degree $\delta_f(s)=m$ (step 1, for the base change along $U'\to S$, $u\mapsto s$). It is the disjoint union of its open subschemes $W'_u=\emptyset$ and $V'_u$ (preimages of $W'$, $V'$; fibres by pasting of cartesian squares [def-pc-fibre-product] with [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product]), so it equals $V'_u$, whose degree is $d$. Hence $d=m$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RY (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-lqf-universally-bounded), line 12761, proof, second paragraph ('After shrinking U ... we may assume V -> U is finite locally free of some degree d, see Morphisms, Lemma 04MH. As u -> s and W_u is empty we see that d = n')

proof.text: *$W'=\emptyset$ and $\varphi(U')\subseteq S_m$; $S_m$ is open.* Let $u'\in U'$ and $s'=\varphi(u')$. The fibre $F=(U'\times_SX)_{u'}$ is finite over $\kappa(u')$ of degree $\delta_f(s')\le m$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-base-change]. It is the disjoint union of its open subschemes $F_W$, $F_V$, the preimages of $W'$, $V'$, which are the fibres of $W'\to U'$ and $V'\to U'$ at $u'$ ([lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], pasting [def-pc-fibre-product]); by the sheaf axiom for the cover $F=F_W\sqcup F_V$, $\Gamma(F,\mathcal O_F)=\Gamma(F_W,\mathcal O)\times\Gamma(F_V,\mathcal O)$, so $\delta_f(s')=\dim\Gamma(F_W,\mathcal O)+m$ (as $V'\to U'$ has degree $m$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]). Hence $\Gamma(F_W,\mathcal O)=0$, so $F_W=\emptyset$ (in a nonempty scheme $1\ne0$ in some local ring, hence in $\Gamma$), and $\delta_f(s')=m$. Since every point of $W'$ lies in the fibre over its image in $U'$, $W'=\emptyset$: $U'\times_SX=V'\to U'$ is finite locally free of degree $m$, and $\varphi(U')\subseteq S_m$. The shrunken etale neighbourhood still contains the distinguished point over $s$, and its whole pullback is finite locally free of degree $m$. This proves the local existence statement; no openness or descent assertion is needed here.
